text:
maya: Quick proposal — pick a 2-tier "critic" setup for the eval harness: a cheap fast critic + a more calibrated heavyweight critic. cheap candidate: llama-2-13b-q4 (8-bit); heavy candidate: llamax-instruct-70b-finetuned (fp16). objective: catch regressions and distributional/bias shifts without too many false positives.
liam: sounds reasonable. what exact metrics should gate CI?
sophia: suggest: consistency (same prompt, different seeds), calibration gap (predicted vs empirical), and disagreement_rate between prod-model and critic. set a soft threshold for CI failures.
liam: concrete numbers?
sophia: start with disagreement_rate > 0.12 => manual review, >0.2 => block. consistency stddev > 0.08 across seeds => warn. calibration gap > 0.06 => warn.
noah: watch out for quantized/8-bit noise inflating disagreement. need a stability probe: run 3 seeds + 2 quant configs and require median verdict stable.
anya: add anchor prompts (small curated set) that must be stable across releases. also propose split-vote resolution: if small critic disagrees with model but big critic agrees, weight big critic 0.7, small 0.3. if consensus_score < 0.6 => escalate to human review.
maya: here's a tiny CI snippet I was thinking we can add to eval-runner: ```bash
# PR-level quick check
eval-runner --suite=smoke_anchors --critic=llama-13b-q4 --thresholds "disagreement:0.12,consistency:0.08"
# nightly heavy check
eval-runner --suite=full_regressions --critics="llama-13b-q4,llamax-70b" --ensemble_weights "0.3,0.7" --escalate_below 0.6
```
liam: nice. how to handle demographic/bias slices? we need synthetic prompt probes and labeled slices in the dashboard.
sophia: we should run adversarial injection (offensive framing + ambiguous contexts) and compute delta metrics per slice. flag any slice whose delta > 2x baseline.
noah: operational note: run heavy critic nightly to save cost, and small critic on PRs. also log token-level latencies and quantization error stats for each critic invocation so we can correlate spikes.
anya: calibration idea — temperature scaling on critic logits per-run; simple formula: p_i = softmax(logits / T) and record T on the dashboard. tune T on the anchor set so calibration_gap minimized.
liam: do we ensemble by averaging logits or by voting? average logits then softmax gives better calibration. voting is simpler but coarser.
maya: agree on logits-averaging for heavy nightly runs; use voting for PR-level quick checks.
eval-bot: CI alert: eval-runner/2034507890 report — disagreement_rate=0.157, consensus_score=0.54, action=escalate (manual review queue).
noah: that looks like a true positive example. can we auto-attach the anchor prompts that caused high disagreement to the ticket?
sophia: yes, include top-5 examples with delta and critic explanations. store them in S3 and link in the ticket.
maya: plan: I'll open an RFC PR with thresholds, CI commands, and instrumentation checklist. @liam @sophia please review. I'll also add a small set of 50 anchor prompts and a script to compute temperature T. :thumbsup:
